summary.text: A lagoon is a shallow stretch of water cut off from a larger body of water by a narrow strip such as a reef, a barrier island or a peninsula.
Lagoons come in two main kinds: coastal lagoons behind barriers on gently sloping shores, and atoll lagoons ringed by coral reefs.
Coastal lagoons are young and short-lived in geological terms, since a fall in sea level can drain them and a rise can let the sea break through.

facts.label: Share of world shores
facts.value: Nearly 15 percent of shorelines have coastal lagoons

facts.label: US East and Gulf
facts.value: Lagoons line more than 75 percent of these coasts

facts.label: Word origin
facts.value: From Venetian łaguna, the waters around Venice

facts.label: Tide limit
facts.value: Coastal lagoons don't form where tides exceed 4 metres

facts.label: Atoll lagoon depth
facts.value: Often have some portions deeper than 20 m

items.prompt: A geologist surveys a coast with steep rocky cliffs plunging into the sea. Why is she unlikely to find a coastal lagoon there?

options.label: The water there is too salty for one
Coastal lagoons need gently sloping coasts
Rocky coasts have no tides at all
Cliffs block all rivers from reaching it

items.explain: Coastal lagoons form on gently sloping coasts where barriers can build offshore; they do not form along steep or rocky coasts.

items.prompt: Why are coastal lagoons usually shallow?

options.label: Fresh water floats on top and evaporates
Coral keeps filling them from below
The coast around them slopes only gently
Tides scour away their deeper parts

items.explain: Coastal lagoons sit on gently sloping coasts, and that gentle slope is why they stay shallow.

items.prompt: Over a long period, the sea level along a coastal lagoon drops well below its old level. What is the likely result?

options.label: The lagoon is left largely dry
The lagoon grows much deeper
The barrier islands get washed away
The lagoon turns into an atoll

items.explain: A relative fall in sea level can leave a lagoon largely dry, while a rise can let the sea breach its barriers.

items.prompt: How does an atoll lagoon come to exist?

options.label: A river mouth floods and is walled off by sand
Waves carve a basin into a rocky headland
A volcano's crater collapses and fills with rain
Coral grows upward as the island it rings sinks away

items.explain: Coral reefs grow upward while the island they surround subsides, until only the reef ring remains above the sea around the water in the middle.

items.prompt: Picture driving the whole US East and Gulf Coasts. Roughly how much of that shoreline has lagoons?

options.label: Under 5 percent
About 15 percent
About 40 percent
More than 75 percent

items.explain: Lagoons are found along more than 75 percent of the US Eastern and Gulf Coasts, far above the world share of nearly 15 percent.

items.prompt: A long bay along a coast runs parallel to the shoreline, while another fills a drowned river valley running straight inland. By Kusky's description, which is the lagoon?

options.label: The drowned river valley running inland
The bay running parallel to the shore
Both, since each one holds sea water
Neither, since both connect to the sea

items.explain: Kusky describes lagoons as normally stretched out parallel to the coast, while estuaries are usually drowned river valleys running across it.
